claim: In the new list view (promRule only, no rulerRule) the Silence menu item is shown via the prom ability, but the silence drawer only renders when `rule` is a Ruler alerting rule, so clicking 'Silence notifications' does nothing.
body:
## [ISSUE] 'Silence notifications' is a dead menu item in the list view

**Severity:** HIGH — users see a Silence action on every Grafana alerting rule in the list and clicking it does nothing.

### The Problem

`GrafanaRuleListItem` now renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` without a `rule` (Ruler DTO). In `AlertRuleMenu`, `canSilence` is `(rulerSilence) || (grafanaSilence)`, and the prom path (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useAbilities.ts:323`) returns `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`, so the menu item is rendered. Its `onClick` calls `handleSilence={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(true)}`, but the drawer is gated here:

```tsx
{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} ... />
)}
```

`rule` is `undefined` in the list view, so the drawer never mounts.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47` passes only `promRule`.
- `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` shows the item whenever `canSilence` is true.
- `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104` requires a Ruler alerting rule to mount the drawer.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before this PR the list loaded the Ruler group, so `rule` was always set and the drawer opened. After it, every Grafana alerting rule in the list shows a Silence item that silently no-ops.

### Research

`SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only needs the rule UID to build the `__alert_rule_uid__` matcher, which `GrafanaPromRuleDTO.uid` provides.

### Recommendation

Let the drawer accept a rule UID (or a prom rule) and render it from either source:

```tsx
const silenceRuleUid = rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)
  ? rule.grafana_alert.uid
  : prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule) ? promRule.uid : undefined;

{silenceRuleUid && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer ruleUid={silenceRuleUid} onClose={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(false)} />
)}
```

If you don't change the drawer, hide the menu item when no Ruler rule is present so the UI doesn't offer an action that can't run.

claim: Pause and Delete are still gated on `rulerRule` being present, so in the list view (which no longer loads Ruler rules) the new prom-based Pause/Delete abilities are computed but never shown, and both actions disappear from the list.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Pause and Delete vanish from the list view even though prom abilities are computed

**Severity:** HIGH — users lose the Pause and Delete actions for every Grafana-managed rule in the new list view.

### The Problem

```tsx
{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (
  <MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ... />
)}
...
{canDelete && rulerRule && ( ... Delete ... )}
```

This PR adds `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` so that `canPause` and `canDelete` can be true from `promRule` alone. But the render conditions still require `rulerRule`. `GrafanaRuleListItem` (and so `FilterView` and `GrafanaGroupLoader`) no longer passes `rulerRule`, so both items are never rendered.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47`: `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` with no `rule`.
- `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:95` passes `rulerRule={rule}`, which is `undefined`.
- The only effect of `grafanaPauseAbility` / `grafanaDeleteAbility` is to flip `canPause` / `canDelete`, which the conditions above then override.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before this PR, `GrafanaGroupLoader` / `GrafanaRuleLoader` fetched the Ruler group, so Pause and Delete were available in the list. After it, both are gone from the list view. The prom-ability work for these two actions is dead code.

### Research

`MenuItemPauseRule` needs the full Ruler rule because pausing rewrites the rule group. `DeleteModal` (via `showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`) only needs the identifier.

### Recommendation

Delete only needs the identifier, so drop the `rulerRule` guard:

```tsx
{canDelete && (
  <>
    <Menu.Divider />
    <Menu.Item ... onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)} />
  </>
)}
```

Widening `handleDelete` to accept `rulerRule?: RulerRuleDTO` makes this type-check. For Pause, make `MenuItemPauseRule` accept a rule UID and fetch the Ruler group lazily when clicked. Otherwise, remove Pause from the prom ability list so the code doesn't suggest the action is supported.

claim: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently on `isAlertingRule`, while the Ruler version used 'any Grafana rule' (including recording rules), so Grafana recording rules lose Export in the list view.
body:
## [ISSUE] Grafana recording rules lose Export (and Pause/Restore) in the prom-based abilities

**Severity:** MEDIUM — recording rules no longer show Export in the list view, which differs from the Ruler-based abilities used everywhere else.

### The Problem

```ts
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, ...],
```

The comment above says "All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition", but `alertingRule` excludes recording rules. The Ruler version it replaces (`useAllRulerRuleAbilities`) uses `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules.

### Theory / Proof

- `utils/rules.ts:133`: `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` covers alerting and recording rules. `.alertingRule` covers only alerting rules.
- In the list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so `canExport` in `AlertRuleMenu` comes only from `grafanaExportAbility`, which is `false` for recording rules.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before this PR, a Grafana recording rule in the list showed "Export -> With modifications". After it, the item is gone. The rule detail page still shows it, because there the Ruler path is used.

### Recommendation

Use the rule-kind check that matches the Ruler version, and keep `isAlertingRule` only for Silence:

```ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, (isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false],
```

claim: The `key={key}` prop was dropped when GrafanaRuleLoader was replaced by GrafanaRuleListItem inside `rules.map`, so Grafana rows have no React key and are reconciled by index as more results stream in.

The rule view link no longer includes `returnTo` (the old component used `createReturnTo()`), so going back from the rule detail page sends users to `/alerting/list` and drops their search and filters.
body:
## [ISSUE] Rule link drops `returnTo`, so users lose list filters when they go back

**Severity:** LOW — a UX regression: users lose their filtered list context when they return from a rule's detail page.

### The Problem

```ts
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`),
```

The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` version was:

```ts
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```

### Theory / Proof

`RuleViewer.tsx:96` uses `useReturnTo('/alerting/list')` for its back navigation. Without the `returnTo` query parameter it falls back to the bare `/alerting/list`, so the current `search` / filter query string is lost. The datasource version, `DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36`, still passes `createReturnTo()`, so Grafana and datasource rows now behave differently.

### Recommendation

```ts
import { createReturnTo } from '../hooks/useReturnTo';
...
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
...
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```
